newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales fall in July except for Renault.
newsitem.headline: French car sales fall in July except for Renault.

text.p: Car sales in France fell 9.7 percent in July, the seventh consecutive monthly fall from inflated 1996 levels, but Renault sales advanced against the trend, the French carmakers committee CCFA said on Friday.
It said new car sales fell to 211,747 units from 234,474 in July 1996, when demand was fuelled by a year-long state car buying incentive scheme.
Stripping out distortions due to the different number of working days, the fall was 5.6 percent, it said in a statement.
PSA Peugeot Citroen car sales in France fell 7.6 percent, but Renault car sales rose 4.1 percent.

Renault's Megane, Clio and Twingo cars were the three best sellers in France last month, a company spokesman said. The Megane five-car family, which includes the hugely popular minivan-styled Scenic, is No. 1 in France this year.
The only other sales gain last month was registered by the Japanese, whose combined sales in France rose 1.3 percent.

The French carmakers, which had been losing ground in their home market, performed better than their foreign rivals. They held 57.6 percent of the market in July, compared with 55.5 percent for the January-July period.
For the first seven months of the year, new car sales were down 21.1 percent in France at 996,265 units.

The French car manufacturers and the CCFA said last month that they expected a 16 percent drop for the year in the French market, which has been weak since the expiry last September 30 of the new-cars-for-old rebates.

Although the July figures marked a vast improvement over June's 30.7 percent plunge, the industry does not expect the trend to reverse before November when the year-over-year comparison will no longer be distorted by the rebates.
The biggest losers in July were Fiat, whose car sales in France fell 40 percent, and Volvo, whose sales dropped 29.5 percent.
